name: Zoora Regime Transition
logic: Enter only when the completed close/EMA200/EMA800 regime changes to +1 or -1. Stop 3 ATR, no target; exit when regime no longer matches. No automatic re-entry after a stop.
rationale: Persistent repricing can produce multi-day directional runs; a slow regime attempts to avoid small fluctuations.
failure: Lag and repeated regime flips in ranges; wide stops commonly exceed $100 minimum-lot budget.
inputs:
input int FastEMA=200; // Alternative 198
input int SlowEMA=800; // Alternative 792
ranges: EMA pairs 200/800 or 198/792 only; 3 ATR stop is fixed in code (a separate trial if changed).

name: Zoora ATR-Band Pullback
logic: In completed H4 Zoora regime, buy a signal bar that touches the H4 fast EMA plus a 0.25 ATR band and closes back above; short is symmetric. Stop StopATR times signal ATR; 2R target; regime-change exit.
rationale: Trend pullbacks may offer lower entry risk than chasing extensions.
failure: An apparent pullback can become a reversal; H4 levels are deliberately delayed until completed.
ranges: BandATR 0.1-0.5; StopATR 1-2.5; EMA pair 200/800 or 198/792.

name: Zoora H4-Level Sniper
logic: Completed H4 Zoora regime. Long H1 range overlaps H4 EMA200 +/-5 pips and closes above prior two H1 highs; short overlaps EMA800 and closes below prior two lows. Signal-bar opens in first three London/NY hours. 12-pip SL, 36-pip TP; completed-close BE at +1R; exit on regime change.
rationale: Combines directional persistence, a pullback to a slow reference level, and local confirmation. This is the least-bad earlier research hypothesis, not an edge.
failure: Only 45 earlier proxy OOS trades, roughly breakeven and cost-fragile; exact execution and UTC/day definitions differ from Python.
ranges: Freeze 12/36 and 5-pip band first; EMA 198/792 is one separately logged sensitivity.

name: Asian Range Expansion
logic: Build complete UTC 00:00-06:00 M5 range. Between range end and first three London hours, enter a new completed-close break beyond the range plus buffer; 12-pip SL, 25-pip TP, max 6h.
rationale: Quiet-session inventory can unwind when London liquidity arrives.
failure: False breaks and news reversals; fixed UTC Asia definition is not local Sydney time.
ranges: Asia end 5-7 UTC; buffer 0.5-2; stop 8-16, target 20-30 pips.

name: London First-Hour ORB
logic: Build the first full London hour from M5 bars, then trade a completed-close escape during the next two hours. Initial stop is max(StopPips, half opening-range width); target 2R.
rationale: The initial high-liquidity auction may define a range whose escape marks committed flow.
failure: Opening-range noise and unusually broad ranges; not equivalent to the pre-London Asian breakout.
inputs: input double BufferPips=1.0;
ranges: Buffer 0-2 pips; minimum stop 8-15 pips. Freeze one London/DST schedule.

name: New York Impulse Continuation
logic: First two NY hours: a fresh candle body >=0.8 ATR, >1.5 times prior body, close in outer 20% of its range and correct side of EMA50. Enter next bar, 10-pip stop/25-pip target, max 90 min.
rationale: Large one-sided opening flow can continue while participants adjust inventories.
failure: Exhaustion candles and news spread/slippage; no future candle confirmation is used.
inputs:
input int TrendEMA=50;
input double BodyATR=0.8;
ranges: BodyATR 0.6-1.2; EMA 30-80; stop 8-12, target 20-30 pips.

name: Prior-Day Extreme Breakout
logic: New completed-close break above prior broker-D1 high or below low, with EMA50 slope aligned. Stop 2 ATR, no target; 35-pip close trail after +1R; max 3 days.
rationale: Daily extremes can attract stop orders and signal multi-session repricing.
failure: Failed breaks, broker day-boundary dependence and overnight swaps.
inputs:
input int TrendEMA=50;
input double BufferPips=1.0;
ranges: Buffer 0-3 pips; EMA 30-100; trail 25-60 pips.

name: Prior-Day Liquidity Sweep Fade
logic: Signal wick sweeps prior broker-D1 extreme by at least buffer, then closes back inside with reversal body. Stop beyond wick plus buffer; target 3R, max 4h.
rationale: An unsuccessful stop-run can trap breakout traders and reverse into the range.
failure: A genuine trend may resume after the rejection; structural stop can be unaffordable.
inputs:
input double SweepPips=1.0;
input double WickBufferPips=1.0;
ranges: Sweep 0.5-3 and wick buffer 0.5-2 pips; fixed 3R first.

name: Donchian 20/10 Turtle
logic: Completed close above previous 20 highs/below lows enters. Initial SL 2 ATR, no target; exit on completed close beyond the opposite prior 10-bar channel; no pyramiding.
rationale: Price channel escape is a simple response to directional persistence independent of EMA levels.
failure: Frequent small range-bound losses and very wide stops for $100.
inputs:
input int EntryBars=20;
input int ExitBars=10;
ranges: Entry 15-55; exit 5-20, always shorter than entry. Sparse prespecified grid only.

name: Bollinger Re-entry Pico
logic: In flat EMA50 conditions (3-bar slope <0.15 ATR), prior close outside 2-sigma Bollinger band and latest close back inside enters toward mean. 5-pip SL/8-pip TP, max 10 min.
rationale: Short liquidity shocks may overshoot a slowly moving local equilibrium.
failure: Costs consume much of an 8-pip target; repeated band-walking in trends.
inputs:
input int BandPeriod=20;
input double BandDeviation=2.0;
ranges: Band period 15-30; deviation 1.8-2.5; SL 4-7, TP 5-10 pips. Require real ticks.

name: Bollinger-Keltner Squeeze Release
logic: Prior 2-sigma Bollinger width lies inside EMA20 +/-1.5 ATR; latest close escapes current Bollinger band and width expands. SL StopATR*ATR; TP 2R; max 6h.
rationale: Compression followed by expansion can reveal new directional information.
failure: Squeezes can persist or release falsely; expansion is not necessarily directional continuation.
valid: BandPeriod>=5 && BandPeriod<=100 && BandDeviation>0.5 && BandDeviation<=4 && SqueezeATR>0 && SqueezeATR<=4
ranges: Band period 15-30; SqueezeATR 1-2; StopATR 1-2; fixed 2R.

name: RSI(2) Trend Pullback
logic: Above EMA200 and prior RSI2 below 10, buy when RSI2 crosses back above 10; mirrored short at 90 below EMA200. SL 2 ATR; no target; exit at RSI2 >=70 long/<=30 short or 2 days.
rationale: A very short oscillator can flag temporary countertrend exhaustion within a slower drift. Connors-inspired, not a reproduction of an equity system.
failure: Pullbacks become trends and RSI thresholds lack a verified forex edge.
valid: TrendEMA>=20 && TrendEMA<=500 && Oversold>0 && Oversold<30 && Overbought>70 && Overbought<100
ranges: Oversold 5-15; overbought 85-95; EMA 100-250. Keep RSI period 2.

name: Keltner Channel Trend Capture
logic: EMA40 slope aligned and completed close crosses EMA40 +/-2 ATR envelope. SL 2 ATR, no target; exit on crossing back through middle EMA; max 5 days.
rationale: Volatility-scaled escape from equilibrium may mark a persistent trend rather than a fixed-pip fluctuation.
failure: Late entries and band break failures; ATR growth expands risk.
inputs:
input int CenterEMA=40;
input double ChannelATR=2.0;
ranges: EMA 20-60; channel 1.5-3 ATR; 2 ATR stop fixed first.

name: MACD Histogram Turn with Slow Bias
logic: MACD(12,26,9) main crosses signal in direction of EMA200 bias and main-line sign. SL StopATR*ATR; 2R target; opposite cross exits; max 6h.
rationale: Momentum reacceleration after a pause can align entry timing with a larger directional drift.
failure: Whipsaw and redundant lagging filters; MACD main minus signal is used, not an MT4-only histogram buffer.
inputs: input int BiasEMA=200;
ranges: BiasEMA 100-250; StopATR 1-2; MACD 12/26/9 fixed initially.

name: Supertrend Volatility Flip
logic: Reconstruct Supertrend(ATR14, multiplier 3) causally over last 200 completed bars. Enter only on direction flip; SL beyond current band (at least 1 ATR); no target; opposite flip exits; max 7 days.
rationale: An ATR-adjusted hysteresis band may stay with direction while suppressing small countertrend noise.
failure: Recursive seed and finite warmup sensitivity; no universal trend persistence.
inputs: input double Multiplier=3.0;
ranges: Multiplier 2-4; ATRPeriod 10-20. Replay length fixed 200; assess seed stability separately.

name: Ichimoku Cloud Escape
logic: Completed close newly escapes above/below the visible cloud, Tenkan above/below Kijun and cloud polarity aligned. SL 2 ATR; no target; close through Kijun exits; max 7 days. No future Chikou comparison.
rationale: Agreement of short, medium and displaced range midpoints may identify persistent directional structure.
failure: Lag, false cloud escapes and sensitivity to market-specific period convention.
ranges: 9/26/52 baseline; assess 8/24/48 as one separate trial. Verify cloud alignment visually.

name: ADX Directional Acceleration
logic: ADX14 newly crosses above 25; dominant DI exceeds other by >=8; close exceeds previous candle high/low. SL StopATR*ATR, TP 2R; exit when ADX <20 or DI dominance reverses.
rationale: Transition from low to stronger directional movement may be more informative than high ADX alone.
failure: ADX is nondirectional by itself and often peaks after much of the move.
ranges: ADX 10-20 periods; Strength 22-30; DI gap 5-15.

name: Inside-Bar Mother-Range Break
logic: Bar2 lies wholly inside bar3 (mother). Bar1 closes outside mother range in direction of EMA100 slope. SL beyond mother opposite extreme plus buffer, TP 3R; max 8h.
rationale: A pause within a directional market can concentrate stops before continuation.
failure: Outside break can exhaust; mother-bar stop often too large for minimum volume.
inputs: input double BufferPips=1.0;
ranges: Buffer 0.5-2 pips; EMA100 fixed; target 2.5-4R only in separately logged trials.

name: Pin-Bar Rejection at Daily Level
logic: At prior broker-D1 high/low +/-3 pips, require wick >=2 bodies and close in outer 30% of range, pointing away from level. SL past wick, TP 3R; max 1 day.
rationale: A strong rejection of a widely watched reference may indicate depleted aggressive flow.
failure: OHLC shapes do not reveal true order flow; strong trends run through levels.
inputs:
input double LevelTolerancePips=3.0;
input double WickBodyRatio=2.0;
ranges: Tolerance 2-5 pips; wick/body 2-3; 3R target fixed.

name: Round-Number Sweep Pico
logic: Sweep and reclaim nearest 50-pip grid level with close at least 0.5 pip back inside. Contrarian entry, 5-pip SL/8-pip TP, max 10 minutes. Grid is explicitly configurable in price-derived pips.
rationale: Clustered orders near 00/50 levels can create temporary overshoot/rejection.
failure: Round numbers can accelerate rather than reverse price; tiny target is cost-sensitive.
inputs:
input double GridPips=50.0;
input double ReclaimPips=0.5;
ranges: Grid 50 or 100 pips; reclaim 0.3-1; SL 4-7 and TP 5-10. For gold configure grid units explicitly.

name: NR7 Volatility Release
logic: Bar2 is strictly the narrowest range of seven bars (2-8). Bar1 closes outside bar2 in direction of EMA50 slope. Structural stop beyond bar2, TP 2.5R; max 6h.
rationale: Volatility clustering can produce expansion after a local contraction; directional slope supplies a separate bias.
failure: Noise in extremely narrow bars; stops may violate broker minimum distance.
inputs: input double BufferPips=0.5;
ranges: Buffer 0.3-1 pips; EMA50 fixed; NR7 fixed rather than mining many lookbacks.

name: Weekly Open Gap Reversion
logic: Compare current broker-W1 opening price with the last completed H1 close before that open. If gap 5-40 pips, during first six elapsed hours require a reversal body toward the old close; target the old close; stop max(8 pips, gap size).
rationale: Weekend inventory imbalances can partially unwind when continuous liquidity returns.
failure: Fundamental weekend news can justify the gap; weekend open and historical quotes vary by broker.
ranges: Gap 5-40 pips; entry window 2-6 hours; session weekday filter means Sunday signals are skipped.

name: ATR Chandelier Trend Runner
logic: EMA50 above/below EMA200 and completed close newly breaks prior 5-bar extreme; initial 2.5 ATR stop, no target; ratchet highest/lowest since entry minus/plus 3 ATR after +1R; exit on bias loss.
rationale: Combines a medium-term trend bias with a volatility-adjusted exit that allows extended runs.
failure: Large initial stops and profit giveback; no claim tight entries can reliably capture 100 pips.
inputs: input double ChandelierATR=3.0;
ranges: Chandelier 2-4 ATR; fixed 50/200 bias and 5-bar trigger initially.

name: Three-Horizon Momentum Agreement
logic: Completed D1 5-bar, H4 6-bar and H1 12-bar returns all agree and exceed 0.5 ATR of their respective timeframes; enter only when H1 momentum newly qualifies. Stop 2 signal ATR; no target; 40-pip close trail after +1R; exit if D1/H4 sign flips.
rationale: Agreement across horizons may reflect broader repricing rather than a single noisy fluctuation.
failure: Correlated filters and late entries; threshold selection easily overfits.
inputs: input double MomentumATR=0.5;
ranges: Momentum threshold 0.3-1 ATR; trail 30-60 pips. Horizons fixed, not interchangeable bar counts.

name: Gold Asian-Range London Retest
logic: Gold-oriented but symbol-generic: build UTC 00-06 M5 range, London first three hours only. Bar2 closes outside range; bar1 retests broken edge within 0.15 ATR and closes back outside. Stop beyond retest wick or StopATR*ATR, whichever wider; TP 3R; max 4h.
rationale: Gold can transition from Asian balance to London price discovery; retest demands acceptance beyond the broken range rather than chasing the first escape.
failure: Gold volatility/spread and contract minimum often make this impossible on $100. Not a gold-only symbol check; pip override mandatory for CFDs.
ranges: Retest 0.1-0.3 ATR; StopATR 1-2; keep gold price-unit override fixed from specification.
